result.keywords: This article examines how fictional archive-practice can be used to reconstruct vanished winter festivals in isolated coastal settlements. It proposes a narrative method for cataloguing oral fragments, lantern imagery, and snowfall records into a single interpretive timeline. A small case study compares three invented village ledgers and shows how seasonal memory is altered by light, drift, and repetition. The work emphasizes cultural preservation, symbolic cartography, and the design of resilient community archives.
result.title: Lantern Drift in Archival Snowfields.
